attributes.cardDescription: The console: three sections, every list a live query, master–detail on a wide canvas.
attributes.readMe:
## What it is
The application shell. Three sections — Work, Knowledge, Setup — organised by the job somebody is doing rather than by card type.

## Three usages
1. **As shipped** — the support console.
2. **A facilities desk** — same shell, Queue/Category/Policy instances swapped.
3. **An approvals centre** — the queue view and its lens strip work unchanged over any card with a deadline.

## The linked example
`ServiceDesk/console` — the Northwind demo world: six tickets across every SLA state, three queues, two policies, two schedules, four articles.

## Non-goals
Not a dashboard and not a report. It is a work surface; aggregate reporting is a separate card.

**Open question.** One realm is one desk; nothing in the schema says so. If two desks ever share a realm, the discriminator belongs on Queue as a scalar, not as a link to this card.

## prefersWideFormat
The host caps a stacked card at 50rem unless the def asks for the full canvas. Without it the master–detail layout collapses to one column and selecting a ticket costs the reader their place in the queue.
